class.name: PlantGenerator
class.brief_description: Generates small meadow plants (rosettes, clover, ferns, sedges, wildflowers) as meshes.
class.description: Builds a plant mesh from a [member preset] and a [member seed], after Prusinkiewicz et al., "The use of positional information in the modeling of plants" (2001): leaves, petals and florets are placed along their axes by phyllotaxis (the golden angle, Vogel's spiral for flower heads, whorls), their size, angle and bend are functions of their position, and leaves, petals and stems are swept along a turtle path. Each seed gives another plant of the same kind. The mesh has one surface per part (leaf, stem, petal, centre) with double-sided materials and back lighting, so light through leaves looks the same in raster and under path tracing. UV2.x holds a wind weight (0 at the root, 1 at the tips) and the vertex colour an occlusion guess. With [member lods], distance LODs are generated as the scene importer does. Use the meshes as [member PlantSpecies.meshes] in a [VegetationField3D]: [codeblock] var gen = PlantGenerator.new() gen.preset = PlantGenerator.PRESET_DAISY gen.apply_preset_colors() species.meshes = gen.generate_variants(3) [/codeblock]

method.name: make_floor
method.description: Returns the forest floor for a stand type as [PlantSpecies], bigger plants first: gap and edge plants in the half-light, shade herbs, mosses, twigs and litter on the closed floor. Each is placed by [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_SHADE] from the placed canopy and, where the stand matters, by [constant PlantSpecies.RULE_CONIFER] (leaf litter under broadleaves, needle litter and bilberry under conifers), so a mixed stand sorts its own floor. Append them to a [Biome] after its trees. The stands match the tree generator's stand types. Each species has the meta [code]floor[/code] set to [code]true[/code]. Brambles and bracken draw impostors past [param impostor_range] metres ([method add_impostors]); 0 keeps their meshes at every distance. The leaf litter is the stand's own fallen leaves ([method stand_litter_leaves]); [param season] is a season state as [code]WeatherMap3D.get_season()[/code] returns it, for the fallen colours and the share of fresh leaves.

method.name: stand_litter_leaves
method.description: The leaves a stand drops, for [member litter_leaves]: one [Dictionary] per broadleaf species with its share of the litter ([code]share[/code]), its leaf form as the tree generator's [code]get_leaf_form()[/code] gives it ([code]kind[/code], [code]count[/code], [code]depth[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]size[/code]), its fallen colour ([code]color[/code]) and the share of fresh leaves among the older litter ([code]fresh[/code]). Forms and, with [param season], colours come from the tree generator when that class is present.

method.name: add_impostors
method.description: Gives a [PlantSpecies] impostors of its meshes ([method make_impostor]): its meshes move to [member PlantSpecies.near_meshes] and are drawn up to [param range] metres, the impostors beyond, with a dithered crossfade. Raster only: under path tracing [VegetationField3D] draws the meshes at every distance, so path tracing keeps the plants' depth and shadows. The species must not have near meshes yet.

method.name: apply_preset_colors
method.description: Sets the colours to the [member preset]'s natural ones.

method.name: generate
method.description: Builds the plant for the current [member preset] and [member seed].

method.name: generate_variants
method.description: Builds [param count] plants with seeds [member seed], [member seed] + 1, and so on.

method.name: make_climber_leaves
method.description: Returns [param variants] single-leaf [ArrayMesh]es of a climber ([constant CLIMBER_IVY], [constant CLIMBER_CLEMATIS] or [constant CLIMBER_HONEYSUCKLE]; [constant PRESET_IVY] reads as ivy), for vines grown by other generators. Each leaf lies in the local XZ plane with its base at the origin, points +Z and is 1 m long; scale it per instance. Each carries the plant material, so it sways, wears, wets and takes snow and light like the ground plants.

method.name: make_impostor
method.description: Bakes an octahedral impostor of a plant (Brucks, 2018): the plant seen from [param frames] by [param frames] directions over the upper hemisphere, each [param frame_size] texels square and fitted to the plant, into an albedo and coverage atlas and a normal, depth and back light atlas. Returns a quad whose shader turns it to the view, blends the three nearest views, and moves each pixel to the plant's surface by the baked depth, so it meets the ground and casts and receives shadows like the mesh. Wind, wetness, snow and [VegetationField3D]'s far thinning work as on the plant shader. The quad has the meta [code]impostor_of[/code] set to [param mesh]. About 2.8 MB of textures with the defaults; baking runs on all cores.

members.member: Colour of flower centres, heads and spikes.

How worn the leaves are, from [code]0.0[/code] (every leaf whole and green) to [code]1.0[/code]: uneven halves, round insect bites out of the margin with dried rims, dead tips on grass-like blades, and older, lower leaves yellowing and browning. Each leaf draws its wear from its own hash, so changing it does not change the plant's shape. The browning travels in the vertex colour's alpha.

For [constant PRESET_LEAF_LITTER]: the stand's fallen leaves ([method stand_litter_leaves]). Each card then carries about two layers of those leaves over its disc, picked by share and shaped by kind: simple, lobed with rounded lobes, palmate, pinnate (mostly loose leaflets, now and then a whole leaf) or digitate. Fresh leaves keep their fallen colour; older ones darken to grey brown and curl. Empty: generic broadleaf litter.
If [code]true[/code], distance LODs are generated (meshoptimizer), so plants far from the camera draw a fraction of their triangles.
Colour of the petals and florets.
Seed of the random variation: each seed gives another plant of the same kind.
Size in pixels of the generated leaf and petal textures.

If [code]true[/code], leaves and petals get generated textures: veins grown by open venation (Runions et al. 2005) with widths by Murray's law, colour drift, dry margins and spots in the albedo, a normal map that sinks the veins, and a translucency map in the back light texture where the veins block light. Textures are baked once per preset, surface and seed variant and shared between meshes.

constants.constant: Dandelion: a rosette of toothed leaves at the golden angle, hollow stalks with a head of florets on Vogel's spiral.
Ribwort plantain: narrow upright leaves and long stalks with dark flower spikes.
White clover: petioles with three round leaflets, sometimes a globe flower head (florets on a Fibonacci sphere).
Fern: arching fronds with alternate lobed pinnae, longest mid-frond.
Sedge: a tuft of narrow V-section blades, sometimes stalks with brown spikelets.
Oxeye daisy: basal leaves, tall stems with a white ray flower and yellow disc.
Meadow buttercup: lobed basal leaves, branching stems with glossy yellow cup flowers.
Stinging nettle: a patch of erect stems with opposite, toothed, heart-shaped leaves and hanging flower strings.
Spear thistle: a rosette of deeply lobed spiny leaves and a branched stem with purple flower heads (first-year plants are rosettes only).
Yarrow: feathery, finely divided leaves and a flat-topped cluster of small white flower heads.
Broad-leaved dock: big wavy-edged basal leaves with red veins and a tall rust-brown seed stem.
Cock's-foot grass: a coarse tussock of broad blades with clustered, one-sided flower heads.
Timothy grass: a tuft of narrow blades with tall stems ending in a dense cylindrical spike.
Last year's dead grass: straw blades, bent, broken and lying flat.
Fallen leaves of several shapes and colours with a few twigs, lying on the ground.
A moss cushion: a low mound packed with upright shoots.
Bilberry: a dwarf shrub of branched green stems with small oval leaves and a few dark berries.
Bracken: a few tall fronds whose triangular, finely divided blades turn nearly flat, for woodland edges and clearings.
Bramble: arching red canes with leaves of three or five toothed leaflets and clusters of dark berries.
Foxglove: a rosette of soft toothed leaves and a tall spike of purple bells hanging to one side.
Common reed: a stand of tall culms with two ranks of drooping grey-green leaves and nodding purplish plumes, for shallow water and wet ground.
Bulrush or cattail: fans of long, twisting strap leaves and stiff stems carrying the dark brown cigar of female flowers with the male spike above, for shallow water.
Soft rush: a dense tussock of glossy leafless stems with pale brown flower clusters bursting from their sides, for wet pasture and marsh.
White water lily: round floating pads with a cleft to the stalk and a few white flowers on the surface. Its origin is the water surface (see [member PlantSpecies.floating]).

Needle litter: loose fallen needles lying across each other and a few cones, the relief over the needle carpet that [method VegetationField3D.get_floor_shader_code] draws on the ground under conifers.
Fallen twigs and small branches lying on the forest floor.
Wood sorrel: carpets of three folded heart-shaped leaflets on slender stalks, with a few white flowers; for shady woods.

Tree seedling: a thin zigzag woody stem with two-ranked oval, wavy-edged leaves, 8 to 75 cm tall; the youngest keep their broad seed leaves, older ones grow flat side sprays from the upper nodes (shade form).
Feather moss: wide, flat, yellow-green carpets as under spruce and pine.
Woodruff: a clonal patch of upright unbranched stems, 12 to 28 cm, with whorls of six to nine narrow leaves held level and small white four-petalled flowers at the top; beech woods.
Wood anemone: single stems with a whorl of three deeply three-lobed leaves two thirds up and one nodding white flower of six or seven tepals; the spring carpet of broadleaf woods.
Ivy as ground cover: creeping runners along the floor with glossy, dark, lobed leaves on stalks turned up to the light, overlapping into a low carpet; oak and ash woods.
Heather: a dwarf shrub of wiry branched woody stems clothed in short leafy shoots, some with spikes of pink-mauve bells; pine heath and acid open ground.
Ivy (Hedera helix): palmate, shallow lobes, dark and glossy with pale veins.
Old man's beard (Clematis vitalba): pinnate, two pairs of ovate leaflets and one at the tip.
Honeysuckle (Lonicera periclymenum): ovate, short-stalked, dull green.
Number of presets.
Beech wood: deep leaf litter, beech seedlings, woodruff, wood sorrel, wood anemone, few ferns.
Oak, lime and ash: a rich herb layer, bramble under the crowns, ivy carpets, wood anemone, ferns, bracken in gaps.
Montane spruce, fir and beech: wood sorrel, ferns and bilberry on mixed leaf and needle litter.
Subalpine larch and spruce: bilberry carpets, heather in the light, few herbs.
Pine heath: bilberry, heather and hair-grass under open crowns, bracken in gaps.
Riparian alder and willow: nettle, sedge and rush near water, ferns.
Hedgerow bottom: bramble, nettle, ivy, foxglove, fern.
Northern hardwoods (sugar maple, beech, birch): deep leaf litter, spring ephemerals, ferns, wood sorrel, many seedlings.
Eastern oak and hickory: oak litter with blueberry and huckleberry carpets, bracken in gaps, few herbs.
White pine and hemlock: deep needle duff, nearly bare; a little moss, wood sorrel and seedlings.
Number of floor stand types.
